source_text:
17.36 Καὶ ἡ παιδεία σου κτλ. Τό· Καὶ ἡ παιδεία σου αὐτή με διδάξει, Θεοδωτίονός
ἐστιν, ἀντὶ τοῦ· Καὶ ἡ παιδεία σου ἀνώρθωσέ με εἰς τέλος, εἰρημένον τοῖς Οʹ.
pass_a_gloss: And the discipline of-you etc. The: And the discipline of-you itself me will-teach, of-Theodotion is, instead of: And the discipline of-you set-upright me into end, having-been-said to-the Seventy.
pass_b_english: The reading “And your discipline itself will teach me” is Theodotion’s, instead of “And your discipline set me upright unto the end,” said by the Seventy.

choices.why: Theodotion’s Greek, not Theodore of Mopsuestia.

choices.english: set me upright unto the end
choices.why: Seventy reading. ἀνορθόω is set upright, not ‘raised me as an end’.
Οʹ is the Seventy, not the ninth psalm or omicron.

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
